name: Chili-Garlic Chicken Rice Bowl with Spicy Pineapple & Bell Pepper Salad (Two Ways)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe was created to feed two adults and two young children. You know your child (their tastes and appetite) best. Use this recipe as a template, adjusting ingredients, cooking methods, and portions as needed.
Using a strainer or colander, rinse the rice under cold, running water, then drain and transfer to a medium saucepan. Add broth and bring the mixture to a boil over high heat.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 cup jasmine rice
2 cups chicken or vegetable broth

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ lime
½ small pineapple
1 avocado
½ pint grape tomatoes
1 jalapeño pepper

instructions.primary_message: Once the liquid comes to a boil, stir the mixture, cover the saucepan, and reduce heat to low. Cook rice until liquid is fully absorbed, 15-18 minutes. Once done, remove rice from the heat and let it stand, still covered, for 5 minutes.
While the rice is cooking, zest and juice lime into a medium bowl.
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl with the lime along with vinegar, chili-garlic sauce, and salt, then whisk to combine the dressing.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 clove garlic
1 tsp apple cider vinegar
½ tsp chili-garlic sauce
¼ tsp salt

instructions.primary_message: Peel, halve, and slice shallot lengthwise into thin strips. Add to the bowl with the dressing.
Cut off skin from pineapple; quarter, core, and medium dice the flesh. Place a ½-cup of pineapple on a plate, then add remaining pineapple to the bowl with the dressing.

Halve and pit avocado; using a spoon, scoop out the flesh. Cut half of the avocado lengthwise into wedges, add to the plate with the pineapple, and set aside. Medium dice remaining avocado and add to the bowl.
Halve grape tomatoes. Add to the bowl.

Quarter jalapeño pepper lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level, then small dice. Add to the bowl, stir to combine the salad, and set aside. (Be careful with jalapeños; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Cut the chicken crosswise into 1/2-inch thick slices and place in another medium bowl. Add cornstarch, salt, and pepper, then toss to coat.
instructions.secondary_message:
680 g chicken thighs, boneless skinless
1 ½ tbsp cornstarch
½ tsp salt
¼ tsp black pepper

instructions.primary_message: Preheat a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Once the skillet is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add chicken and cook, flipping once, until cooked through and crispy on both sides, 5-6 minutes. Remove from heat.
Meanwhile, using a clean cutting board, roughly chop peanuts.
When the chicken is done, add a ⅔-cup to the plate with the pineapple and avocado. Add peanuts, chili-garlic sauce, and fish sauce to the skillet with the remaining chicken and stir to combine.
instructions.secondary_message:
2 tsp chili-garlic sauce
2 tsp fish sauce

instructions.primary_message:
FOR THE KID PLATES: Divide 1 cup of rice, diced pineapple, avocado wedges, and plain chicken between plates. 

FOR THE ADULT PLATES: Divide remaining rice, salad, and spicy chicken between plates or bowls. Enjoy!
